 Wales and Portugal meet in the final round of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League group stage on Tuesday, 17 November, at 19:45 (UK time). The match takes place in Cardiff, with both teams looking for a positive result for different reasons.
 Portugal have already secured their place in the quarter-finals but need to avoid defeat to guarantee top spot in Group A4. Wales, meanwhile, are certain to finish bottom after losing four of their five matches, although a draw would secure their place in the relegation playoffs.

 Wales vs. Portugal - Head-to-head record
 Wales and Portugal have met twice in major competitive fixtures, with the Portuguese winning both encounters without conceding a goal .
 Their first meeting came in the semi-finals of Euro 2016, when Portugal secured a 2-0 victory on their way to winning the tournament.
 The two nations met again in September 2026, when Portugal claimed a narrow 1-0 home win in the opening round of the Nations League.
 That record gives the visitors a clear advantage ahead of Tuesday’s encounter, although Wales will be hoping to make home advantage count as they seek their first goal and first positive result against Portugal.

 Wales – Dragons Fighting to Secure a Relegation Playoff Place
 Wales enter their final Nations League fixture after a disappointing campaign that has left them bottom of Group A4. However, they still have an opportunity to secure a place in the relegation playoffs. Let’s examine their recent form and expected line-up.
 Recent form
 Wales have collected just three points from their opening five Nations League matches, recording one victory and four defeats . Craig Bellamy’s side began with consecutive losses to Portugal and Denmark before securing a 2-1 home win over Norway.
 However, the Dragons were unable to build on that result, losing 1-0 at home to Denmark before suffering a 3-1 defeat away to Norway on Saturday. Despite some encouraging attacking moments in Oslo, Wales were unable to prevent another defeat and are now guaranteed to finish bottom of the group.
 Bellamy’s side have won just once in their last nine matches across all competitions, recording three draws and five defeats. Nevertheless, they remain well placed to secure a relegation playoff spot, with a draw against Portugal guaranteeing that outcome regardless of results elsewhere.
 Wales will be without Ethan Ampadu, who is suspended, while Neco Williams is unavailable through injury. Josh Sheehan could replace Ampadu in midfield, with Connor Roberts expected to start at right-back. David Brooks is also pushing for a starting place after scoring against Norway.

 Portugal – Visitors Looking to Secure Top Spot
 Portugal have already qualified for the Nations League quarter-finals after winning four of their opening five matches. However, their recent defeat to Denmark means they still have work to do to finish top of Group A4.
 Recent form
 Portugal began their Nations League campaign with four consecutive victories , beating Wales 1-0, Norway 2-1, Denmark 4-2 and Norway again by a 2-1 scoreline. Those results put Jorge Jesus’s side in a commanding position at the top of the group.
 However, their winning run came to an abrupt end on Saturday, when Denmark secured a surprising 4-1 victory in Portugal. The hosts found themselves four goals behind by the 75th minute, exposing defensive vulnerabilities that had also been evident in earlier matches.
 Despite that setback, Portugal have already secured their place in the quarter-finals. They now need only a draw in Cardiff to guarantee first place in Group A4, although another defeat could allow Denmark to overtake them. Portugal have kept just one clean sheet under Jesus, which came in their opening Nations League victory over Wales.
 The visitors will be without Ruben Dias, who is suspended, with Antonio Silva expected to replace him in central defence. Jesus could also make changes in midfield, bringing Joao Neves and Bernardo Silva into the starting XI, while Goncalo Ramos is expected to lead the attack.

 Predictions for Wales vs. Portugal - visitors to dominate
 Portugal will be looking to bounce back after their surprising 4-1 defeat to Denmark, while Wales have struggled defensively throughout the competition. Portugal to win the first half is an appealing option, particularly given their superior attacking quality.
 However, Portugal have conceded in each of their last four Nations League matches, suggesting that Wales could also create opportunities. Both teams have reasons to push for a positive result, making over 1.5 goals in the first half another market worth considering.
 Despite their recent setback, Portugal remain the stronger team and have won both previous meetings with Wales. The hosts’ defensive vulnerabilities could provide opportunities for the visitors to secure a convincing victory, so our main prediction is Portugal to win with a -1.5 Asian Handicap .
